title: Zesty Dense Ethiopian Lamb Injera
description: A traditional Ethiopian dish featuring lamb, injera, and a blend of spices, with a dense and slightly bitter texture, made satvik-friendly by using no onions or garlic, and cooked to perfection using sous-vide techniques.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the injera flour and water to make the injera batter, stirring until smooth and free of lumps.
Let the injera batter rest for 24 hours to allow it to ferment.
Preheat the sous-vide machine to 130 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a separate bowl, mix together the ground lamb, ground cumin, coriander powder, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Divide the lamb mixture into 4-6 portions, depending on desired serving size.
Place each portion of the lamb mixture into a sous-vide bag, sealing tightly to prevent leakage.
Cook the lamb in the sous-vide machine for 2 hours, or until it reaches an internal temperature of 130 degrees Fahrenheit.
Once the lamb is cooked, remove it from the sous-vide bags and place it on top of the injera batter, which has been poured onto a heated skillet or mitad.
Cook the injera for an additional 1-2 minutes, until it is crispy and golden brown on the bottom.
Serve the zesty dense Ethiopian lamb injera hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.
